summary: Harivallabh Chunilal Bhayani was an Indologist and linguist. He earned degrees at Samaldas Arts College and Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan, completing his doctorate under Muni Jinvijaya. He held professorships at Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan and Gujarat University, later directing the L.D. Institute of Indology.

Harjot Oberoi works in religious studies, history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at St. Stephen's College, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the Australian National University before holding the Chair of Punjabi and Sikh Studies at the University of British Columbia from around 1987.

Harogadde Manappa Nayak was an Indian scholar in linguistics and Indology. He served as Director at the University of Mysore from circa 1967 to 1984 and as Vice-chancellor of Gulbarga University between 1984 and 1987.

Harold C. Conklin was a linguist and anthropologist. He studied at the University of California, Berkeley and Yale University. He taught at Columbia University and served as a professor at Yale (1962–1996) and curator at the Peabody Museum of Natural History (1974–1996).

Harold G. Coward is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who earned his doctorate from McMaster University. He served as a professor at the University of Calgary (ca. 1973–1992) and as director at the University of Victoria (ca. 1992–2004).

Harold Hargreaves was an archaeologist and Indologist. He served as headmaster of Government High School, Amritsar, and held multiple positions with the Archaeological Survey of India, including Superintendent of the Frontier Circle and Deputy Director General (1928–1931).

Harold Scheub earned degrees from the University of Michigan and the University of Wisconsin-Madison, also studying at UCLA. After teaching at Valparaiso University and Masindi Senior Secondary School, he served as a professor of humanities at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (ca. 1970–2013).
Harold Stewart was an Australian scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied at the University of Sydney and the Sydney Conservatorium of Music.

Harold Walter Bailey was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological linguistics. He studied at the University of Western Australia and Oxford under Frederick William Thomas. He taught at SOAS before holding the Sanskrit chair at Cambridge University (1936–1967).

Haroon Khan Sherwani was a historian and Indologist who studied at Aligarh Muslim University and the University of Oxford, mentored by Ghulam Yazdani. He held posts at Osmania University (~1919–1945), Nizam College (~1945–1948), and Zakir Husain Delhi College (~1948–1951).

Harry Falk is an Indologist, archaeologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Gaya Charan Tripathi. He taught at the University of Freiburg (~1980–1990) and served as professor and director at the Free University of Berlin from 1993 to 2012.

Hartmut Buescher is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Copenhagen under Chandrabhal Tripathi and held posts at the University of Copenhagen and the Royal Danish Library.
Hartmut Scharfe was an Indologist and linguist who completed his doctoral studies under Paul Thieme and held an academic post at the University of California, Los Angeles.

Hartmut-Ortwin Feistel was an Indologist who held positions at the Royal Library of Berlin's Oriental Department and directed projects at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities, also editing the Verzeichnis der orientalischen Handschriften in Deutschland.

Haruhiko Masaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Gakushuin University and completed master's and doctoral courses at the University of Tokyo, later serving as a professor at Nagasaki University from approximately 1977 to 2003.
Haruka Yanagisawa was a historian and Indologist who held academic posts at the University of Tokyo from around 1993 to 2007 and at Chiba University.

Harumi Hirano Ziegler is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. She earned her MA and PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles, completing her doctorate under the supervision of Robert E. Buswell Jr.

Harunaga Isaacson is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Groningen and Leiden University under Tilmann Vetter and Hans T. Bakker, and held posts at Oxford, the University of Pennsylvania, and the University of Hamburg.

Harushige Kōzu was a linguist who studied under Naoshiro Tsuji at the University of Tokyo and at Oxford. He taught at the University of Tokyo (1938–1948) and served as professor and dean of humanities at Musashi University from 1968.

Harvey B. Aronson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed his doctoral studies under Richard Hugh Robinson. He served as a professor at the University of Virginia and co-directed the Dawn Mountain Center for Tibetan Buddhism.
